### The Thorns That Belonged to Us
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-april-16-2025.html
Passage: Matthew 27:29-30
Points:
- Roman soldiers severely brutalized, beat, and ridiculed Jesus as a mock monarch.
- Thorns first entered creation in Genesis as the outward sign of the curse of sin.
- By bearing the crown of thorns, Jesus took upon Himself the pain, sorrow, and judgment that belonged to us.
- Remembering that Christ endured this agony in our place gives believers comfort and perspective in trials.

### Pilate Presents Jesus to the Crowd
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier.org
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/pilate-presents-jesus-to-crowd
Passage: John 19:1-5
Points:
- Pilate subjected Jesus to flogging and soldier mockery in an attempt to appease the crowd.
- Bringing Jesus out in a purple robe and crown of thorns, Pilate announced, "Behold the man!"
- Without realizing it, Pilate pointed to Jesus as the ideal, sinless representative of humanity.
- True humanity is revealed in Christ, providing believers an example of humility, truth, and righteousness to follow.

### Behold the Man!
Author: Trevin Wax
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/trevin-wax/behold-the-man/
Passage: John 19:5
Points:
- Pilate unknowingly spoke profound theological truth when he presented the battered Savior to the crowd.
- Just as Adam was created on the sixth day and brought judgment, the second Adam reversed the curse on that same day.
- Jesus received the crown of thorns and mock robe to take humanity's guilt and shame upon Himself.
- Rather than a mere man grasping at divinity, He was the Son of God embracing human suffering to bring redemption.
